subject: HealthBridge security follow-up: VPC / air-gap options and next steps
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.inference>
To: Laura Myers <laura@healthbridge.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: HealthBridge post-call recap: VPC vs air-gapped options & immediate asks

Hi Laura —

Thanks again for the time earlier. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we can move this into procurement: 

- SOC 2 status: you mentioned the security team wants evidence of our current SOC 2 (Type II) timeline and scoping. We are SOC 2 in progress; our most recent report was Type I in 2026 and Type II expected Q3 2027.
- Data residency / GDPR / HIPAA: Redwood supports EU region deployments and our Private offering can be configured to meet HIPAA requirements with BAA + Private VPC.
- Deployment modes you asked about: Hosted API (fastest), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools), Private (VPC or on-prem/air-gapped). For HealthBridge’s regulatory posture, Private VPC + optional air-gap for model weights was discussed.
- Network diagram request: you asked for a sketch showing minimal inbound surface and where the data sits (control plane vs compute). I’m attaching a quick sketch (redwood_network_sketch_v1.pdf) and the vendor questionnaire so your team can begin filling answers.

Action items I propose (next steps):
1) Security team to confirm whether HealthBridge requires a fully air-gapped deployment or VPC with strict egress controls.
2) HealthBridge to return the vendor security questionnaire (attached).
3) Redwood to provide an ops-level diagram and a BAA template once we confirm deployment option.
4) Tentative follow-up: 30-minute technical deep-dive with your infra/security folks — are mornings PST better for you?

Attachments: [Attachment: HealthBridge_Vendor_Security_Questionnaire.pdf (PDF, 420KB)], [Attachment: redwood_network_sketch_v1.pdf (PDF, 120KB)]

Thanks — I’ll coordinate on the follow-up invite after we hear back from your security lead.

— Aisha
Aisha Rahman
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
aisha_rahman@redwood.inference
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Laura Myers <laura@healthbridge.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.inference>
Cc: security@healthbridge.com, dpo@healthbridge.com
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: HealthBridge post-call recap: VPC vs air-gapped options & immediate asks

Hi Aisha —

Thanks for the clear recap and the attachments. Quick notes from our side after the call:

- SOC 2: We need a copy of Redwood’s most recent SOC 2 Type I report + evidence of controls in scope (until Type II is available). Can you provide the Type I report and a short control mapping?
- Air-gap vs VPC: Our legal/regulatory group prefers to avoid a full air-gap if possible due to maintenance overhead. Preference is VPC with strict egress controls and optional physical isolation for model weights if needed later.
- Questionnaire: I’ve added the security alias on this thread. They will triage the vendor security questionnaire — please expect follow-up questions about key management, key rotation, and audit log retention.

We can do the 30-minute deep dive Thursday morning PST. I’ll ask security to prepare a short list of focused questions so we don’t go long.

— Laura
Laura Myers
Director, Infrastructure & Security, HealthBridge Medical
laura@healthbridge.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>
To: security@healthbridge.com, dpo@healthbridge.com, Laura Myers <laura@healthbridge.com>
Cc: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: HealthBridge post-call recap: VPC vs air-gapped options & immediate asks

Hi team —

Thanks, Laura — quick follow-up from our side on the specifics you flagged so your security team can triage:

- SOC 2 artifacts: attaching our SOC 2 Type I summary and a short control mapping doc. We’ll redact any customer-specific info and can route the full auditor produced report through an NDA channel if needed.
- Key management: Redwood supports customer-managed keys (KMS) for Private deployments. For Hosted/Dedicated we offer envelope encryption and can integrate with AWS KMS / Azure Key Vault when deployed in customer VPCs.
- Audit logs & retention: By default we retain operational audit logs for 365 days for Private deployments. We can extend retention and produce specific exports for compliance requests.
- Network sketch: our attached sketch shows the control plane remaining in Redwood-managed control (optional private control plane offering is available for enterprise customers). Compute nodes for Private VPC deployments are in-customer subnets.

Attachments: [Attachment: Redwood_SOC2_TypeI_Summary.pdf (PDF, 180KB)]

Next: If security can drop a short prioritized list of questionnaire items (top 10 blockers), we’ll have engineering answer them ahead of the Thursday deep-dive.

Best,
Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>

Team —

Reviewed the thread and Ben’s attachments. Approving the upstream asks:

- Go ahead and share the SOC 2 Type I summary with HealthBridge under our standard vendor disclosure NDA (we have a template).
- Engineering to prepare the engineering-focused answers to the top 10 questionnaire items — aim for EOD Friday so we can iterate with HealthBridge before the deep-dive.
- Coordinate scheduling: Aisha, propose three time slots for Thursday morning PST and include a short agenda with the top 5 security topics.

If HealthBridge sticks with VPC + strict egress, we should also prepare a short cost delta estimate vs fully hosted so procurement has the numbers. Ben — can you draft a back-of-envelope?

Marissa
